label: Curves
notes: Open the chapter. A Riemann surface is a one-dimensional complex manifold; a smooth complete algebraic curve over the complex numbers is the same data. The deck follows printed pages 212 through 363 and develops divisors, line bundles, Riemann-Roch, the canonical map, the Abel-Jacobi theorem, and the Jacobian variety.

label: Divisors and Line Bundles
notes: Define divisors on a curve. A divisor is an integer combination of points. Linear equivalence classes form the Picard group, which is the disjoint union of components indexed by degree. The degree-zero component is an abelian variety, the Jacobian. Every line bundle on the curve is the bundle associated to some divisor class.

label: Riemann-Roch
notes: State the Riemann-Roch theorem. For a divisor D on a curve of genus g, the dimension of H zero of L D minus the dimension of H zero of K minus D equals degree D minus g plus one. The theorem balances sections against obstructions; the canonical divisor K is the dual partner.

label: Canonical Map
notes: Introduce the canonical map. For curves of genus g at least two, the canonical divisor gives a map to projective space of dimension g minus one. The image is the canonical curve. Hyperelliptic curves are the exception: their canonical map factors through a degree-two cover of the projective line.

label: Abel-Jacobi
notes: Sketch the Abel-Jacobi theorem. Choose a base point; the map sending a degree-zero divisor to its integral of holomorphic differentials lands in the Jacobian. The theorem asserts this map is an isomorphism between the degree-zero Picard group and the Jacobian. This is the bridge between algebra and complex tori.

label: Jacobian
notes: Describe the Jacobian variety. It is a complex torus of dimension g, principal polarized by the Theta divisor. The geometry of theta functions, Torelli's theorem, and the Schottky problem all study this object. The chapter introduces the Jacobian and prepares the reader for the deeper structural results in chapter 03.

label: Recap
notes: Close with the chapter summary. Curves carry divisors, divisors give line bundles, Riemann-Roch balances sections against obstructions, the canonical map embeds non-hyperelliptic curves, Abel-Jacobi identifies divisors with points on the Jacobian. These are the working tools for one-dimensional algebraic geometry.
